LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Meta.Meta__Description: The Parametric Scrapbook: scripted sheet elements that are dragged onto the paper like any scrapbook item and then keep answering to their parameters, the way an AutoCAD dynamic block does. Owned by Na__LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__.js (the engine); each element type has a module of its own and a block of its own here. A parametric element lands as an ordinary group of vectors and text, so it moves, copies, prints, exports and undoes like anything drawn by hand; the group record carries a Group__Parametric block, which is what lets it be regenerated. Ungrouping it explodes it: the vectors and text stay, the parameters go.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Meta.Meta__Block: Group__Parametric : { Parametric__Type, Parametric__Version, Parametric__Params, Parametric__Link }. The element's place on the paper is never stored: the Move tool and a paste shift a group's members and know nothing of this block, so the generator always writes the element's origin as the first point of its first member and the engine reads it back from there.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Meta.Meta__HouseTitle: The drawing title was measured on 19-Sep-2026 from the six elevation titles and two plan titles Adam lettered by hand on PS02 D22 and D21. All eight agree: capitals, qualifier first (EXISTING EAST ELEVATION), Open Sans 600 at 3.5 mm in #172b3a, ranged left; an underline 0.4 pt thick and exactly 60 mm long, 1.631 mm under the baseline and 0.171 mm in from the text's left; and the scale bar 6.318 mm under the underline, sharing its left end. He groups title, underline and bar as one object.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Meta.Meta__HouseBar: The scale bar was measured on 19-Sep-2026 from the twelve bars Adam drew by hand on PS02 D21 Floor Plans and D22 Elevations (A2, 1:50). All twelve agree: five cells of 20 mm in two rows of 1 mm, the top row filled on odd cells and the bottom row on even ones, fill #666666, edge #172b3a at 0.2 pt, an empty cell with no fill at all; Open Sans 400 numerals in #172b3a centred on each division with their baseline 5.314 mm under the bar, 2.5 mm at the two ends and 2 mm between. THE FILL WAS LIGHTENED ON 20-Sep-2026 to #858585 - a fifth of the way from the measured #666666 to white - because Adam found the checker too heavy on the page. Nothing else about the bar moved, and the test fixtures carry the new value.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Meta.Meta__BarRight: A SCALE BAR PLACED TO THE RIGHT was measured on 20-Sep-2026 from the arrangement Adam laid out by hand over PS01's proposed south east elevation: the title and its underline exactly where they always are, and the bar standing away along the same line with its FOOT on the title's baseline - 3.631 mm (1.631 + the bar's own 2) above the underline - so the two read as one band across the foot of the drawing. Its far end is meant to land under a corner of the building above it, which is why that end is the one that is dragged and the near end is the one that lengthens.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Meta.Meta__Portal: THE PROJECT PORTAL BLOCK (21-Sep-2026) is drawn from two mock-ups Adam made: a narrow column - code, Scan Me button, heading, bullets - and a wider one that stands that column beside a heading and a paragraph. Its code is NEVER encoded here: the box is one vector carrying a Shape__Qr block, and the shape painter fills it with whatever symbol the Project QR Code system answers for the project on screen, which is the same symbol the title block prints. So a block dragged onto a sheet carries THIS project's code, and one copied into another project carries that one's. The size of the code is the parameter (20 mm as shipped, the rest of the list on the lookup grip); everything round it is set in paper millimetres and does not scale with it, because type on a drawing is house sizes or it is wrong.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Meta.Meta__Infill: THE CABINET INFILL (21-Sep-2026) was measured from the vector PDF of NP03 D07 Rev C (First Floor Plans, 31-Mar-2026) and the LayOut Core Scrapbook Adam drew it from - five Storage infills and a Shelving one on that sheet, all alike: a cross corner to corner of the cupboard, #333333 at 0.15 pt, dashed 0.9 pt on 0.9 pt; the name in Open Sans Regular 6 pt #333333, centred in a #fcfcfc box under the same dashed rule; the box 2 pt (0.706 mm) clear of the words at each end and 3.034 mm deep, the baseline 0.856 mm below its middle. An infill taller than it is wide has its words turned to read UP the sheet. Its size is paper millimetres, never tied to a drawing: dropped on one, a tile is sized at that drawing's scale from Element__RealSizeMm.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Eleme.Elements__Description: The tiles the Parametric Scrapbook section shows, in this order. An element is a PRESET of a type: Element__Type names a registered element module, Element__Id is the element's own (two elements may share a type; without one it is the type), Element__Params are laid onto every element dropped from it, and Element__PreviewParams are added for the tile and the drag ghost only - a title's tile reads EXISTING EAST ELEVATION where a real drop reads its own viewport. Element__DrawingTypes lists the drawing types an element is offered on ('siteplan', 'architectural'); an element without the key is offered on every sheet. Elements__TypeNames is what each type is called on the sheet's group tag and in the panel.

Elements__List.Element__Description: The title under a drawing, with its underline and scale bar, written by the drawing it is tied to: Existing or Proposed from the model that drawing draws, and North, East, South or West from the north set in the 3D model. Until north is set an elevation reads {{DIRECTION}}. Drag the round socket onto another drawing to retitle it.

Elements__List.Element__Name: Drawing Title + Scale Bar to the Right
Elements__List.Element__Description: The same title, with its scale bar stood away along the same line instead of under it, for a wide elevation whose bar belongs under its far corner. Drag the arrow at the bar's FAR end to carry it along - it snaps to the corners of the drawing above - and the arrow at its NEAR end to lengthen it back towards the title. Its position also steps 50 mm at a time from the panel.
The title and its underline alone, written by the drawing it is tied to. Drag the arrow at the underline's end to lengthen it; the scale bar can be switched on in its settings.

A checker scale bar that reads the scale of the drawing above it. Drag the arrow at its far end to lengthen it; click the triangle at its zero end for another scale; drag the round socket onto another drawing to tie it to that one.

The project's own QR code, big enough to see across a table, with a Scan Me button and the few lines that make somebody want to point a phone at it. The code is this project's and fills itself in. Click the triangle for another size - 20 mm as dropped - or for the version with the full description beside it.

The same block with a heading and a paragraph beside it, for a cover sheet or a presentation drawing. Drag the arrow at the end of the paragraph to set how wide the words are set; click the triangle for another code size.

Every room measured on this sheet, under its group with a subtotal, and the total at the foot. It re-writes itself whenever a room is drawn, renamed, regrouped or stretched. Drag the arrow to set how wide it is set; click the triangle for one group only, for square feet, or for the summary form.

One row per group - Ground Floor, First Floor, Garage - with its total and the whole sheet's total. The summary a planning statement quotes. The groups are made in the Floor Areas panel by filing each room under one.

The dashed cross and boxed name that say what a cupboard is: Storage as dropped, and Services, Full Height Storage, Wardrobes, Pantry Unit or Shelving from its triangle - or words of your own in its settings. It is dropped by its bottom left corner, which snaps onto a corner of the cabinet; then drag any other corner onto the one opposite. The white fill underneath is off, so the cabinet's own lines show through; switch it on to blank them out.
Elements__List.Element__RealSizeNote: Width and height in real millimetres, drawn at the scale of the drawing the tile is dropped on: 36 x 12 mm on a 1:50 plan, 18 x 6 on a 1:100 one. Dropped anywhere else it is the block's own WidthMm x HeightMm.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Scale.ScaleBar__Description: Element one: the scale bar. See Meta__HouseBar for where every size below came from.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Scale.ScaleBar__MinLabelSpacingNote: Divisions closer together than this on the paper are not all numbered: every second, fifth or tenth is, and the two ends always are.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Scale.ScaleBar__TargetNote: What a scale that is not in ScaleBar__Standards is solved towards: the 1, 2, 2.5 or 5 x 10^n division nearest TargetDivisionMm on the paper, and the count of them nearest TargetLengthMm.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Scale.ScaleBar__MenuScaleNote: The scales the lookup grip's menu and the panel offer. The first four are the app's architectural scales (1:200 joined them on 21-Sep-2026; it was here first because a street elevation wants it) and the last two its site plan ones. Any scale in ScaleBar__Standards can be added.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Scale.ScaleBar__StandardsNote: What a bar is put back to when its scale changes. DivisionMm and SubdivisionMm are real-world millimetres; Units is what the numerals count in ('m' or 'mm'). Every row is a 100 mm bar, and all but 1:1, 1:2, 1:20 and 1:200 are the house 5 x 20 mm.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__Description: Element two: the drawing title (Na__LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__DrawingTitle__.js). See Meta__HouseTitle for where every size below came from. The origin is the underline's left end; the text stands above it and the scale bar hangs below. The words themselves - Existing, Proposed, Elevation and the two placeholders - belong to 20__System__Viewports/Na__LayoutEditor__ViewportIdentity__Config__.json, and the compass words to 46__System__NorthDirection/Na__North__AppConfig__.json, because the editor names unnamed elevation viewports in the same words.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__UnderlineNote: UnderlineMm is the LEAST the underline is: sixty millimetres underlines EXISTING EAST ELEVATION with room to spare. With GrowsToFit on, the line ALWAYS runs PastTextMm beyond the end of the words - measured from where the text starts (TextOffsetXMm) plus its width - and is rounded up to a tenth of a millimetre. StepMm is what the stretch grip moves it by when the title has no scale bar.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__UnderlinePastTextNote: Adam, 21-Sep-2026, over RB05's long elevation titles: 'make sure this line always goes at least 5 mm past... because it looks kind of weird being short.' PAPER millimetres, like every size in this block, so it is 5 mm on the sheet at every scale - 500 mm of building at 1:100, 250 at 1:50. Until then the line stopped a hair past the last letter (FitExtraMm), which read as flush, and a title rebuilt before the paper's text metrics had loaded stopped ten per cent SHORT of it: the chrome's estimate is an average width, and capitals are wider than average. The engine now rebuilds any title whose underline no longer ends where this rule puts it, once those metrics are in.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__UnderlineBarGapNote: The one thing allowed to shorten that run: a scale bar stood to the RIGHT, whose numerals hang across the underline's level at its zero end. The run past the words stops BarGapMm short of the bar's zero end rather than strike through them - but never short of the words themselves (their width plus FitExtraMm, the length the line was drawn to before the rule). A bar below, or none, never shortens it.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__BarPlacementNote: Where the scale bar sits. 'below' is the house title Adam letters by hand: the bar 6.318 mm under the underline, sharing its left end. 'right' stands it away along the same line instead - see Meta__BarRight - for a wide elevation whose bar belongs under its far corner. A title with no bar at all ignores this.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__ScaleBarAboveUnderlineNote: How far the bar's TOP stands ABOVE the underline when it is placed to the right. 3.631 = TextBaselineAboveUnderlineMm + the bar's own 2 mm, which puts the bar's foot exactly on the title's baseline.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__BarOffsetNote: Where the bar's ZERO end stands when it is placed to the right, measured from the element's OWN ORIGIN - the underline's left end - and never from the end of the underline, so retitling a drawing can lengthen the underline without shoving the bar off the corner it was put under. StepMm is what the panel's spinner and a free drag of the far arrow move it by; a drag that lands on a snapped vertex is exact and ignores the step. MaxMm is a paper limit, comfortably past the long edge of an A0.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Drawi.DrawingTitle__PhaseModeNote: auto reads Existing or Proposed off the model the drawing draws; existing and proposed force the word; none leaves it out.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__Description: Element three: the Project Portal block (Na__LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__ProjectQr__.js). See Meta__Portal for where it came from. The origin is the top left corner of the code's box; the button, the caption, the heading and the bullets run down from it, and the full form's heading and paragraph stand to its right. The SYMBOL is not here and is not in the record: the box carries a Shape__Qr block and the shape painter asks the Project QR Code system (02__Src__AppModules/53__System__ProjectQrCode/) for the project's own code every time the sheet is drawn.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__SizeNote: The symbol edge to edge, in paper millimetres, and the ONLY thing that makes this block bigger or smaller. 20 mm is what a block dropped from the Scrapbook starts at - Adam, 21-Sep-2026 - more than twice the 8.8 mm the title block prints, and still a detail on the sheet rather than the sheet. It was 30 until then; a block already placed keeps the size it was given. The list is what the lookup grip's triangle and the panel offer, and it runs 15 to 30 - the sizes that sit on a drawing beside other things. 40 and 50 were dropped because at that size the code stops being a detail on a sheet and starts being the sheet, and the type round it, which is house sizes and does NOT grow with the code, reads as an afterthought against it. Every size here is far above what a phone needs - a 29 module symbol at 15 mm is a 0.52 mm module against the 0.28 mm floor - so the limits are about the page, not the camera, and the shape painter reports the printed size to the QR system's own check either way. A block already set to a size that has left the list keeps it: only the menu changed, and Normalise still holds anything between SizeMinMm and SizeMaxMm.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__MarginFractionNote: The clear paper inside the box, as a fraction of the code rather than a count of millimetres - which is what keeps the quiet zone at the same number of MODULES whatever size the code is drawn at. 0.07 of a 29 module symbol is 2.03 modules, the two the QR system asks for, and a longer address (a bigger symbol, more modules) only ever gives it more. The box's own rule sits at the edge of that margin and counts as not clear, which is why the rule is where the margin ends and not inside it.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__ButtonPadNote: The least paper between the handset-and-words pair and the end of the stadium. The button is the code box's width OR the pair plus twice this, whichever is more: the label is a house size and does not shrink with the code, so at 15 mm the pair is wider than the box and a button locked to the box wore its own words out of both ends. At 20 mm and above the content fits inside the box's width and the button is exactly the box, as it always was.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__ButtonIconNote: The handset is a MODERN SMARTPHONE, drawn the way the phone in somebody's pocket looks: a slim body about half as wide as it is tall, well-rounded corners, and the Dynamic Island pill filled in across the top of the screen. The first glyph was a squat rounded box with a bar across its foot, which Adam found too ambiguous to read as a phone (21-Sep-2026) - at this size it could have been a door, a battery or a tablet. The pill is what says 'phone' at 4.6 mm; its size and place are fractions of the width, set in the module.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__ButtonNote: The Scan Me button: a stadium the width of the code's box, with a handset and the words centred in it as one pair. It is not a control and nothing happens when it is clicked - it is the thing that tells somebody who has never met a QR code that the square above it is for pointing a phone at, which is the whole reason this block exists rather than the title block's code being left to do the work.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__GapsNote: EVERY GAP BELOW IS BASELINE TO BASELINE, not a space between two lines - which is the only way to set type that stays even when one line is a heading and the next is a caption. A gap therefore has to carry three things: the descender of the line above, the air wanted between them, and the CAP HEIGHT of the line below (0.72 of its size in Open Sans). A 4.6 mm gap under a 3.5 mm heading leaves 1.3 mm of air; the same 4.6 under the 5.4 mm title leaves none at all, which is what had the project name sitting on the title's descenders. The numbers here were re-set on 21-Sep-2026 against a rendering of both forms at 30 mm, and the title has a gap of its own for exactly that reason. They were set again the same day for the smaller type Adam asked for with the 20 mm default - body text (the paragraph AND the bullets) 2.2 mm, the caption 1.5 - keeping the air between lines roughly what it was: bullets 3.6 apart (1.5 mm of air), paragraph lines 3.4 (1.3 mm).
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__CaptionNote: Measured from the FOOT OF THE BUTTON, not from a baseline, because the button is a shape and has no baseline to measure from. 2.8 leaves 1.7 mm of paper between the button's rule and the caption's capitals, now the caption is 1.5 mm (Adam, 21-Sep-2026; it was 2.1 under a 3.6 gap). The caption is ranged LEFT on the column's own edge like everything under it: centred on the code box it overhung that edge at every size where the wording was wider than the box - which is every size below 25 mm - and an element whose left edge moves with its code size cannot be lined up with anything on a sheet.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__NameNote: The project's name, under whichever heading leads the block: the compact form's own, and the full form's larger one. It is read live from the project on screen, so renaming the project rewrites every block in the pack; a name typed into the panel wins and stops it following, and clearing that box puts it back. It is lettered ONCE - the full form's left-hand column leaves it out, because the heading beside it is already carrying it and saying it twice reads as a mistake.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__TitleNameGapNote: The full form's title is 5.4 mm where the compact form's heading is 3.5, so the drop to the project name underneath cannot be the same number in both. This is the title's own: 5.8 baseline to baseline leaves 1.9 mm between the title's descenders and the name's capitals. NameGapMm stays what the compact heading wants. One number under two different sizes of type is the fault this key exists to undo.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__BodyWidthNote: How wide the full form's paragraph is set, in paper millimetres, measured from the left edge of its own column. The stretch arrow at the end of the paragraph drags it in 5 mm steps and the words re-wrap as it moves. MaxMm is a paper limit, comfortably inside the long edge of an A0.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__CaptionText: Use your phone or tablet camera
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__CaptionTextNote: Said in plain words on purpose. Anybody under forty points a camera at a QR code without being told; the people this drawing is put in front of - a client, a neighbour, a planning officer - very often have not, and 'Scan Me' alone assumes they know what to scan it WITH.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__BodyText: Point your phone or tablet camera at the code and the whole building opens in 3D. Walk through it at full size, step between the saved views and scenes, measure anything you like, and read every drawing live online. Nothing to download - it opens straight in your browser.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__BodyTextNote: Written to be scanned, not read: what to do, what happens, and the one objection that stops people - having to install something. It names no app and no system, because what is being offered is the building, not the software.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Proje.ProjectQr__BulletsNote: One line each, in the order somebody would care about them, and short enough that the column stays the width of the code's box and a little over. They are lettered exactly as written here - no capitalising, no full stops - so the wording is entirely this file's.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__Description: Element four: the area schedule (Na__LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaSchedule__.js), which reports what the rooms measured on a sheet add up to. Two forms of one type: 'areas' is a row per room under its group heading with a subtotal, and 'groups' is a row per group - the summary a planning statement quotes. The origin is the LEFT END OF THE TOP RULE, with the title above it and the rows below, as the drawing title's origin is the left end of its underline. THE NUMBERS ARE NOT HERE AND ARE NOT TYPED: they arrive as the Data parameter, filled from the sheet's own index by 59__Feature__FloorAreas, so a table always says what the drawing beside it says.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__WidthNote: How wide the table is set, in paper millimetres: the name runs from the left edge and the figure is ranged right at the far edge, so this is the distance between them. 78 mm is a column that sits comfortably beside an A2 title block. The stretch arrow drags it in 2 mm steps.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__TextNote: House type sizes. EVERY VERTICAL MEASUREMENT BELOW IS TAKEN AS A RATIO TO TextSizeMm, so changing the type size in the panel sets the whole table larger or smaller without any of it colliding.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__RuleNote: Two weights and no more: the 0.4 pt rule under the title and above the total, and a 0.2 pt hairline under the column heads. A table on a drawing is read by its numbers, and a box round every cell reads as a form to fill in.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__SwatchNote: The colour chip at the head of a row is the same colour the room is washed with on the drawing, which is what lets somebody read the table against a coloured plan without a legend. Switched off from the lookup grip for a table that is going to be printed in black.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__EmptyLabel: No areas measured on this sheet
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__CrossedNote: What is printed instead of a figure for a room whose outline crosses itself. Such a run has no honest area - the shoelace subtracts one lobe from the other - so a number is never shown for it, here or on the room itself.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__AreaS.AreaSchedule__UnitsNote: British planning drawings are in square metres, so that is what leads: 'both' writes 18.45 m² (199 ft²), for a client or an agent who thinks in feet. These are the SCHEDULE'S own settings - the label written in the middle of each room has its own, in the Floor Areas config - so a table can quote feet while the plan stays metric.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__Description: Element five: the cabinet infill (Na__LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__CabinetInfill__.js) - the dashed cross and boxed name that say what a cupboard on a plan is. See Meta__Infill for where every figure below was measured. It is held by its bottom left corner - the tile hangs from it, the drop snaps it, and a hollow grip there moves it - and each of the other three corners is a grip that moves its corner with the one opposite held, snapping to the drawing's corners. (Inside, the origin is still the top left corner; paper y runs down.) Paper millimetres throughout, and never tied to a drawing.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__SizeNote: Paper millimetres. WidthMm x HeightMm is what a tile is dropped at anywhere but on a scaled drawing, where the element's Element__RealSizeMm is used at that drawing's scale instead. A corner dragged free steps both sides by SizeStepMm from the corner held; a corner snapped to a vertex of the drawing is kept exactly.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__LabelsNote: The words the triangle and the panel offer, in this order, and Label is what a dropped infill says. Adam's five from his brief, and Shelving, which his own screenshot of the house infill labels. Anything else is typed in the panel's Own words box, which wins over the list until it is cleared. An infill keeps the words it was given if this list changes.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__TextNote: 6 pt is 2.1167 mm: LayOut's size, kept to four places so the box a tile draws is the one on NP03 to the thousandth (8.978 mm round Storage, 3.034 deep).
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__LineNote: The cross, and the rule round the box: 0.9 pt dash, 0.9 pt gap in the PDF, which is 0.3175 mm - the line style record keeps two decimals. A thin dashed dark grey is what reads as a light mid-grey dotted line on the paper; a paler colour at this weight all but disappears.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__BoxNote: LayOut's text box, hugging its words: PadEm clear of them at each end (2 pt at 6 pt), HeightEm deep for one line (3.034 mm at 6 pt) and one line height deeper for each line after, the first baseline BaselineBelowCentreEm below the middle of a one-line box (0.856 mm at 6 pt). All three are fractions of the text size, so a bigger label gets a bigger box. The fill is so near white that it reads as paper; it is what stops the cross running through the words.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__FitNote: The words run along the infill's longer side unless told otherwise, and break at their spaces over as many as MaxLines lines - as evenly as they will go - when they would come within LabelClearMm of either end of the cabinet. LineSpacing is used only when the editor cannot say its own (the Text setup's LineSpacing, which the label is drawn at).
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Cabin.CabinetInfill__FillNote: The fill underneath is OFF as dropped: the cross and the label alone, so the cabinet the model draws shows through. Switched on, a rectangle of this colour, with no rule, lies under the cross and blanks out whatever is under the infill. It is an ordinary vector - open the group and give it any colour to match a background, and the element keeps that colour through every rebuild after, as it keeps anything else restyled by hand.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Viewp.ViewportLink__Description: The link between a parametric element and a viewport (Na__LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__ViewportLink__.js). AutoLinkOnInsert links a dropped element to the nearest 2D viewport, measured from the drop point to the viewport's frame; MaxLinkDistanceMm is how far away that viewport may be. A scale bar sits under a drawing's title, which sits under the drawing, so the frame is usually 10 to 30 mm above it. FollowScale regenerates a linked element when its viewport's scale changes, inside the same undo step.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Grips.Grips__Description: The grips a selected parametric element shows. Sizes are screen pixels, held at any zoom like every other grip. Each grip stands its OffsetPx clear of the point its element type gives it, in the direction that type says: for a scale bar the stretch grip off the far end and the lookup grip off the zero end, both level with the middle of the bar.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Grips.Grips__SlideNote: The slide grip is the double arrow off the FAR end of a scale bar placed to the right of its title. It carries the bar along the line without changing its length, snapping to the projected linework so the end can be put under a corner of the drawing above; the stretch arrow at the bar's near end then lengthens it back towards the title, its far end held where the slide left it. SnapGuidePx is the dashed line drawn from a snapped vertex down to the bar while a slide is held.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Grips.Grips__PlugNote: The plug is the handle on the noodle's FAR end, where it lands on the drawing it is tied to. It is dragged to another drawing exactly as the socket is, for people who reach for the end of the cable rather than the element it comes from.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Noodl.Noodle__Description: The link noodle (Na__LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__LinkNoodle__.js): the curve from a selected element's round socket to what it is tied to, and the outline round that. Px values are screen pixels, held at any zoom. Reach is how far each end of the noodle runs before it turns, in paper millimetres: half the distance between the ends, held between the two limits. ScaleCellInsetMm is how far into the title block's Scale cell the noodle lands for an element tied to the sheet's scale.

LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__Description: The Parametric Scrapbook's wording. {name} is an element's name, {scale} a scale as the title block writes it, {viewport} a viewport's name, {target} what an element is tied to.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__LibraryHint: Dynamic elements. Drag one onto the sheet, or double-click it; select it afterwards for its grips and its settings.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__LibraryReadOnly: Elements can only be placed while sheets are editable.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__LibraryFailed: The parametric scrapbook could not be read, so it has no elements.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__ItemTitle: {name}: drag onto the sheet, or double-click to place it in the middle of the view.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsExplode: Ungroup it (Ctrl+Shift+G) to explode it into plain vectors and text.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsNeedsNorth: {{Direction}} fills itself in once north is set in the 3D model: Dev Tools, North Direction, Draw Compass.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsNeedsLink: Tie it to a drawing to fill {{Drawing}}: drag its round socket onto one.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsTitleTyped: Typed by hand, so it no longer follows its drawing. Clear the box to go back to automatic.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsTitleNamed: The drawing's viewport has a typed name, which the title uses. Clear that name and the title is written from the model and north.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsTitleStorey: Written from the plan's storey, which is chosen per floor plan in the 3D view: Dev Tools, Floor Plans, Storey.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsBarOffsetNote: From the title's left edge to the bar's zero end, in 50 mm steps. On the sheet, drag the double arrow at the bar's far end to carry it along - it snaps to the corners of the drawing above - and the arrow at its near end to lengthen it back towards the title.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__ToastUntiedTitle: Untied. It keeps what it says.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsQrSizeNote: How big the QR code itself prints. Everything round it is a fixed size, so the block grows only by its code.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsQrWidthNote: How wide the paragraph is set, in 5 mm steps. On the sheet, drag the arrow at the end of it.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsQrTyped: Typed by hand, so it no longer follows the project. Clear the box to go back to automatic.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsQrNeedsName: {{Project}} fills itself in once the project's data has loaded. Type a name here to letter one now.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsQrCode: The code is this project's own, and is the same one the title block prints. It fills itself in - there is nothing to choose.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsAreaEmpty: No rooms have been measured on this sheet yet. Draw one with the Floor Area tool (A) and this fills itself in.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__GripStretchWords: Drag to set how wide the words are set
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__GripCorner: Drag this corner - the corner opposite stays put. It snaps to the drawing's corners
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__GripBase: Drag to move it by this corner - it snaps to the drawing's corners
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsInfillTyped: Typed by hand, so the list no longer sets it. Clear the box, or pick from the list, to go back.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsInfillOnDrawing: {width} x {height} mm on the drawing at {scale}. Drag the hollow grip at its bottom left corner onto a corner of the cabinet, then any other corner onto the one opposite - both snap to the drawing.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsInfillOffDrawing: Paper millimetres. Drag the hollow grip at its bottom left corner onto a corner of the cabinet, then any other corner onto the one opposite - both snap to the drawing.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__PropsInfillKept: Anything restyled inside the group - a colour, a line weight, the dashes - is kept when it is rebuilt.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__GripStretchBack: Drag towards the title to lengthen; the far end stays put
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__GripSlide: Drag to carry the bar along - it snaps to the corners of the drawing above
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__GripLink: Drag onto a drawing to tie this to it, or onto the title block for the sheet's scale. Let go on bare paper to untie it.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__GripPlug: Drag this end onto another drawing to move the tie there, or onto the title block for the sheet's scale. Let go on bare paper to untie it.
LayoutEditor__ScrapbookParametric__Label.Labels__ToastNoViewport: No 2D viewport is near enough to link to.
